standard_prerequisites: Context span 3050-3059: R is a ring with an ideal I such that R/I is a finite flat module but not projective (explicit example delivered as card L48315, section-finite-flat-not-projective); this means I is not finitely generated (Algebra, finitely-generated-pure-ideal) and I = I^2 (Algebra, pure); the base scheme is S = Spec(R)
Context span 3062-3065: the ring map R -> R + (R/I)epsilon with epsilon^2 = 0 is finite, flat, not of finite presentation, with all fibre rings complete intersections and geometrically irreducible

Context span 3068-3073: A = R[x, y]/(xy, ay for a in I) is as an R-module the direct sum of R y^i (i >= 0) and (R/I) x^j (j > 0); R -> A is flat finite type not of finite presentation, each fibre ring isomorphic to kappa(p)[x, y]/(xy) or kappa(p)[x]

Context span 3076-3082: B = R[X_0, X_1, X_2]/(X_1 X_2, a X_2 for a in I) gives Proj(B) -> S proper flat not of finite presentation with fibres P^1_s or the vanishing locus of X_1 X_2 in P^2_s (a projective nodal curve of arithmetic genus 0)

Context span 3085-3090: M = R + R + R/I, B = Sym_R(M), X = Proj(B): X -> S is proper flat not of finite presentation with geometric fibres P^1_s or P^2_s, in particular smooth and geometrically irreducible
core_obligations: Item 1: the dual-numbers map R -> R + (R/I) epsilon from the context is flat finite type, not of finite presentation, with complete intersection geometrically irreducible fibres

Item 2: R -> A from the context is flat finite type, not of finite presentation, with fibres kappa(p)[x, y]/(xy) or kappa(p)[x], which are geometrically connected, geometrically reduced, dimension 1, complete intersections
Item 3: Proj(B) -> S from the context is proper flat, not of finite presentation, with fibres P^1_s or the vanishing locus of X_1 X_2 in P^2_s
Item 4: Proj(Sym_R(M)) -> S from the context is proper flat, not of finite presentation, with fibres P^1_s or P^2_s
